title: A life in Alexandria
description: A fictional life born in Alexandria in 66 BCE. Learn a trade, study, build a household or try rare military and court careers. Childhood death risks are reduced for playability; adult risks retain the disclosed later Roman Egyptian female comparison model. Personal events, career odds and stat effects are authored game rules, not measured historical frequencies.

stayed.label: Made a home in the city

army-service.label: Has served in the royal army

district-grain-delivered.label: The new grain order was carried out

protected-granary.label: Assigned troops to protect grain stores

royal-service-ended.label: Royal service ended under Roman rule

joined-alexandrian-war.label: Took part in the Alexandrian War

origins.title: A merchant household
origins.text: You are born into a household that runs a small shop near the harbor. Relatives and neighbors help with your care.

origins.title: An artisan household
origins.text: You are born into a household of craft workers. The family shares workspace, tools and the care of a new child.

origins.title: A harbor household
origins.text: You are born into a household that earns money from work on the quays. Adults fit your care around shifts and deliveries.

mortality.description: Background death risks begin with the Roman Egyptian female comparison table in Zakrzewski (2015), Table 1. The historical comparison's converted annual death probabilities are reduced for gameplay before age 18: age 0 uses 15% of the comparison probability, ages 1–4 use 7.5%, and ages 5–17 use 15%. Ages 18 and older retain the comparison probabilities. This makes about 95% survive their first year and about 91% reach age 18 before optional dangerous choices are considered. These are authored game-balance assumptions, not reconstructed Alexandrian mortality rates. Adult probabilities from age 18, the 95+ tail and age-100 cap retain the prior rules. These are authored gameplay risks, not measured death rates for a male born in Alexandria in 66 BCE. Health and Resources do not alter background risk. Explicitly dangerous choices can add their stated fatal outcome.

jobs.title: Quay porter
jobs.description: Carry and sort cargo near the harbor. Open to a beginner, with tiring work and a modest return.

jobs.title: Potter
jobs.description: Shape and finish everyday vessels in a workshop. Practical training brings steadier work.

jobs.title: Merchant's clerk
jobs.description: Keep lists and check small accounts. Reading and practical numeracy both matter.

jobs.title: Workshop copyist
jobs.description: Copy and check written work patiently. There is more learning than immediate wealth.

jobs.title: Merchant sailor
jobs.description: Work aboard a merchant ship. The return comes with hard work and time away from familiar people.

jobs.title: Small-shop keeper
jobs.description: Manage goods, customers and accounts. Experience helps, but responsibilities leave less time for company.

jobs.title: Ceramic decorator
jobs.description: Finish and decorate pots and mould-made figures in a workshop.

jobs.title: Wood carver
jobs.description: Carve small figures, fittings and patterns in wood.

jobs.title: Sculptor
jobs.description: Make small figures and carved reliefs for customers. Larger commissions need more experience.

jobs.title: Philosophy tutor
jobs.description: Teach small groups, read arguments and help pupils explain their reasoning.

jobs.title: Sky-table calculator
jobs.description: Copy observation tables and check calendar calculations. Access to texts depends on personal contacts.

jobs.title: Astrologer
jobs.description: Prepare charts and explain traditional interpretations. These are historical beliefs, not reliable predictions.

jobs.title: Royal army soldier
jobs.description: Drill, guard stores and carry out orders in the Ptolemaic army. Service is available before Roman rule.

jobs.title: Royal army officer
jobs.description: Organise a small unit and keep its equipment and supply records. A commission requires a separate appointment.

jobs.title: Royal army general
jobs.description: Hold a senior field command. This is an exceptional appointment; training alone does not secure it.

jobs.title: Royal court adviser
jobs.description: Prepare petitions and proposals for royal officials. Appointment depends on rare patronage, not just qualifications.

partners.name: Demetria
partners.description: Demetria makes everyday pottery in a workshop. She is patient at work and often jokes with the other workers.

partners.name: Thais
partners.description: Thais sells goods at the market and knows many of the regular customers. She likes hearing news from travelers.

partners.name: Berenike
partners.description: Berenike works with linen and often shares meals with friends after work. She is quick to offer help with a task.

partners.name: Tyche
partners.description: Tyche copies documents in a workshop. She enjoys reading unfamiliar material and asking how things work.

outcomes.text: You pay for time with a patient reader and practise the marks until they become a little more familiar.
A trader lets you work through small counts and check them again. The lesson costs time and resources.
You work through a small task under supervision. Tired hands and a little spoiled material are part of the lesson.
You practise knots, loads and the movements expected aboard a ship. Repetition teaches more than watching from the quay.
You arrange to start work as a quay porter and pay for a few initial supplies.
You arrange to start work as a potter and pay for a few initial supplies.
You arrange to start work as a merchant's clerk and pay for a few initial supplies.
You arrange to start work as a workshop copyist and pay for a few initial supplies.
You arrange to start work as a merchant sailor and pay for a few initial supplies.
You arrange to start work as a small-shop keeper and pay for a few initial supplies.
Your practiced eye helps you prepare a clear copy of a difficult page. The extra payment comes after long, tiring hours.

activities.text: Check a complicated set of accounts

outcomes.text: You work patiently through counts and payments until the figures agree. Extra responsibility brings a return and a long day.
Experience helps you finish a demanding order. The work pays, but leaves tired hands and less time for company.

activities.text: Take responsibility for a shipboard watch

outcomes.text: Your experience earns you a more responsible watch. You learn from the work, though the hours leave you weary.
You step away from regular work. There is time to recover and reconsider, while the household must manage with less.

activities.text: Ask Demetria to begin a courtship

outcomes.text: Demetria agrees to begin a courtship. You arrange to spend more time together.
Demetria declines the courtship. You return home without making plans together.
You and Demetria marry. You pay for a modest meal and set up a shared household.
You and Demetria share a meal and talk about the past few days.

activities.text: Ask Thais to begin a courtship

outcomes.text: Thais agrees to begin a courtship. You arrange to spend more time together.
Thais declines the courtship. You return home without making plans together.
You and Thais marry. You pay for a modest meal and set up a shared household.
You and Thais share a meal and talk about the past few days.

activities.text: Ask Berenike to begin a courtship

outcomes.text: Berenike agrees to begin a courtship. You arrange to spend more time together.
Berenike declines the courtship. You return home without making plans together.
You and Berenike marry. You pay for a modest meal and set up a shared household.
You and Berenike share a meal and talk about the past few days.

activities.text: Ask Tyche to begin a courtship

outcomes.text: Tyche agrees to begin a courtship. You arrange to spend more time together.
Tyche declines the courtship. You return home without making plans together.
You and Tyche marry. You pay for a modest meal and set up a shared household.
You and Tyche share a meal and talk about the past few days.
You and your spouse separate and divide the household belongings. Any children you have remain listed as your children.
A child is born. You choose a name, buy supplies and take turns with the care.
You do not have a child this year. You spend a little on preparations.

activities.text: Spend an evening with the household

outcomes.text: You put the remaining tasks aside and share a meal with the household.

activities.text: Help your children with their tasks

outcomes.text: You set work aside to help your children and pay for a few things they need.
You buy learning materials and arrange for someone to explain the parts your children find difficult.
You leave paid tasks for another day, sleep longer and eat at home.
You take a short walk, stop in the shade and return before you are tired.
You bring a little food and spend the afternoon catching up.
You make deliveries for several stalls and collect small payments.
You replace worn straps and practise a stronger fastening. A repaired pair can be used again.
You count jars and baskets, then check the total with the seller. They pay you a little for the help.

activities.text: Cook a meal for the household

outcomes.text: You buy ingredients, prepare the meal and eat with the household.

activities.text: Clean and refill the water jars

outcomes.text: You scrub the jars, rinse them and fetch fresh water. The work takes most of the morning.

activities.text: Take an extra daytime cargo shift

outcomes.text: You move cargo with a crew in daylight. The extra pay comes with sore arms and less rest.
You share food, listen to songs and learn a verse that the others know.

activities.text: Move heavy cargo at night (risk of death)

outcomes.text: The load is moved without an accident. You collect extra pay and sleep through most of the next morning.
A load shifts in the dark and injures your leg. You miss work while it heals.
A heavy load slips from its ropes and crushes you. You do not survive the injuries.

activities.text: Swim beyond the harbor steps (risk of drowning)

outcomes.text: You swim out from the steps and return. The current is stronger than you expected, and you need a long rest.
A current carries you away from the steps. You cannot reach the shore, and nobody reaches you in time.
You shape a few small vessels, dry them and help check a kiln load.
You mark a pattern and carve it slowly. A worker helps you correct the uneven parts.

activities.text: Model a figure and practise a relief

outcomes.text: You model a small figure and practise cutting a shallow relief in spare material.

activities.text: Study an argument with a teacher

outcomes.text: You listen to an argument, ask questions and try to explain the reply in your own words.

activities.text: Record the Moon and compare sky tables

outcomes.text: You record a position of the Moon and compare the entry with a copied table. You stay up late to finish.

activities.text: Compare zodiac signs and traditional readings

outcomes.text: You copy a sky diagram and compare several traditional interpretations. The exercise does not establish that the predictions work.
You practise formation changes and equipment care under supervision. Your arms ache afterward.
You prepare a short speech, deliver it to a small group and answer their questions.
You arrange work as a ceramic decorator and buy a few supplies.
You arrange work as a wood carver and buy a few supplies.
You arrange work as a sculptor and buy a few supplies.
You arrange work as a philosophy tutor and buy a few supplies.
You arrange work as a sky-table calculator and buy a few supplies.
You arrange work as a astrologer and buy a few supplies.
You enlist, receive equipment and begin guard duties and drill.

activities.text: Apply for an officer's post (15% appointment chance)

outcomes.text: An officer recommends you for a vacant post. You receive a commission and take charge of a small unit.
No commission is offered. You return to your current duties.

activities.text: Seek an army command (2% appointment chance)

outcomes.text: A patron backs your appointment to a senior field command. You receive written orders and a staff to organise.
The command goes to someone else. You keep your officer's post.

activities.text: Seek a court appointment (3% appointment chance)

outcomes.text: A patron recommends your petition. You receive a post preparing proposals for royal officials.
Your petition is received, but no appointment follows. You keep your present work.
You finish the painted vessels, check the firing and deliver the order.
You measure the damaged fitting and carve a replacement that fits the opening.
The customer approves the figure after you adjust its surface and repair a chipped edge.

activities.text: Lead a discussion of competing arguments

outcomes.text: You ask each speaker to explain their argument, then compare their reasons with the group.
You find a copying error, check the arithmetic and prepare a corrected table.
You compare two readings with the same chart. Their claims differ, and you record the disagreement rather than treating either as a proven prediction.
You run through changes of formation, check equipment and repeat the parts that went wrong.
You check loads and direct carts to the right stores while other troops guard the route.

activities.text: Propose a grain-delivery change (10% adoption chance)

outcomes.text: Officials accept your delivery schedule and issue an order to move grain to the district you named.
The officials leave the existing schedule in place. You keep your notes for another proposal.

activities.text: Present a district petition to a clerk

outcomes.text: You explain a blocked access lane, present the residents' names and obtain a date for an inspection.

character.deathCauseDescription: Natural-death cause labels are fictional explanations selected after the comparative all-cause mortality draw; they add no extra annual hazard. Causes marked choiceOnly are used only when an explicitly dangerous choice or activity draws its fatal outcome. Those outcome weights are authored game risks, not measured historical rates. Neither cause labels nor risk weights come from the cited mortality sources. Family-planning ages, job returns and skill thresholds are also authored game balances.

deathCauses.title: An illness in early childhood
deathCauses.text: You become seriously ill while very young. Your household cares for you, but you do not recover.

deathCauses.title: A severe fever
deathCauses.text: You develop a severe fever. It gets worse despite care, and you do not recover.

deathCauses.title: A sudden abdominal illness
deathCauses.text: You develop severe abdominal pain and weakness. The illness worsens and becomes fatal.

deathCauses.title: An illness of the chest
deathCauses.text: A serious chest illness makes breathing difficult. You do not recover.

deathCauses.title: An injury at work
deathCauses.text: An accident at work causes serious injuries. You do not survive them.

deathCauses.title: An accident at sea
deathCauses.text: You suffer a fatal accident while working aboard a ship.

deathCauses.title: Caught in the Alexandrian fighting
deathCauses.text: You are caught in the Alexandrian fighting and suffer fatal injuries.

deathCauses.title: An illness in later life
deathCauses.text: You grow weaker during an illness in later life. Your household cares for you until you die.

deathCauses.title: A sudden illness
deathCauses.text: You become ill and get worse quickly. You do not recover.

deathCauses.title: Smoke inhalation in a warehouse fire
deathCauses.text: You went into a burning warehouse to help someone. The smoke overcame you before you could get out.

deathCauses.title: Swept overboard in rough weather
deathCauses.text: You chose to sail in bad weather. A wave swept you overboard, and the crew could not reach you.

deathCauses.title: Crushed by a cargo load
deathCauses.text: You took a heavy cargo shift at night. A load slipped from its ropes and caused fatal injuries.

deathCauses.title: A fatal wound during a robbery
deathCauses.text: You chose to fight the people demanding your purse. One of them wounded you, and you did not survive.

deathCauses.title: A severe illness after unsafe water
deathCauses.text: You used water from a dirty jar. You became severely ill afterward and did not recover.

deathCauses.title: Drowned during a swim
deathCauses.text: You swam beyond the harbor steps. A current carried you away from shore, and you could not get back.

deathCauses.title: A fatal wound in the Alexandrian fighting
deathCauses.text: You volunteered for a forward post during the fighting. A weapon wound proved fatal.

events.title: Fighting in Alexandria
events.text: Caesar arrives in 48 BCE during the struggle for Egypt's throne. Fighting breaks out in Alexandria and reaches streets near the harbor.

events.title: The city's water during the war
events.text: The war continues into 47 BCE. A Roman account describes attempts to cut Caesar's water supply and the digging of wells.

events.title: News from Actium
events.text: News arrives that Antony and Cleopatra's forces lost at Actium in 31 BCE. Octavian now has the advantage in the war.

events.title: Egypt under Roman rule
events.text: Ptolemaic rule ends in 30 BCE and Egypt comes under Roman control. Augustus later lists the addition of Egypt among his achievements.

events.title: You are born
events.text: You are born in Alexandria in 66 BCE. The adults in your household decide how to share your care.

choices.text: Share the care within the family

outcomes.text: Your relatives take turns feeding, holding and settling you.

choices.text: Ask a trusted neighbor to help

outcomes.text: A trusted neighbor helps with feeding and care. Your household pays for a few supplies.

events.title: Your first steps
events.text: You take a few steps between two adults. They keep their hands close when you start to wobble.

events.title: Playing in the courtyard
events.text: Other children play outside your door. Your caregivers decide whether to let you join them or keep you close to home.

choices.text: Stay close to the household

outcomes.text: You play near the adults and help put small things away.

choices.text: Spend time with the neighbors' children

outcomes.text: You play with the other children and come home with dusty feet.

events.title: Learning a few letters
events.text: A neighbor offers to teach you a few letters. Lessons cost time and a little money, and your household still needs help with its work.

choices.text: Take reading lessons

outcomes.text: You practise until you can recognize and copy a few letters.

choices.text: Help with practical work

outcomes.text: You watch a worker, try a few small tasks and learn how to handle the tools.

events.title: Around the neighborhood
events.text: You learn the routes to nearby shops, workshops and quays. You can now finish a few errands without asking for directions.

events.title: Training for work
events.text: Your household looks for someone to teach you. Reading, workshop training and helping at home are the options available.

choices.text: Practise reading and counting

outcomes.text: You practise reading short passages and checking simple counts.

choices.text: Learn beside an experienced craft worker

outcomes.text: You spend time at a workbench, preparing materials and practising basic tasks.

choices.text: Help more at home

outcomes.text: You take over more errands and household tasks. The extra help saves money.

events.title: Your first paid work
events.text: Someone offers you work carrying loads on the quays. You can take the pay or look for a task that gives you more practice.

choices.text: Take porter work on the quays

outcomes.text: You start carrying and sorting cargo on the quays. You are paid, but the loads leave you tired.

choices.text: Look for a task that teaches you more

outcomes.text: You help with an unfamiliar task. The pay is small, but you get more practice.

events.title: Choosing a regular job
events.text: You can take porter work nearby. A sailor's job needs Seamanship 15, and a copyist's job needs Literacy 30. Training in Your life can help you qualify.

choices.text: Take porter work close to home

outcomes.text: You take regular porter work nearby. A few useful contacts help you find more jobs.
You take porter work nearby. The first payments are lower than you expected.

choices.text: Take a sailor's place with the ship's crew

outcomes.text: You join the crew and sail out of the harbor. The work pays, but you spend less time at home.
You join the crew. The first crossing leaves you tired, and other sailors help you learn the tasks.

choices.text: Become a copyist in the workshop

outcomes.text: You start at a copyist's workshop. You copy short passages and check them with another worker.

events.title: A message home
events.text: A returning sailor can carry a message home. You can pay a writer to help or spend the day looking around the port.

choices.text: Send a long message home

outcomes.text: You send news about the work, the port and the people you have met.

choices.text: Spend the day learning the port

outcomes.text: You walk the quays and find the shops and landing places you need.

events.title: A damaged page
events.text: A damaged page reaches the workshop. An experienced copyist offers to work through it with you, but other paid work is also available.

choices.text: Work beside an experienced copyist

outcomes.text: The copyist shows you how to check the damaged words. You finish part of the page together.

choices.text: Take paid work instead

outcomes.text: You finish the paid task and put the money aside. You leave the damaged page for another day.

events.title: A neighbor needs help
events.text: A neighbor asks you to arrange a small job. You can help for free or agree on a payment.

choices.text: Make time for your neighbor

outcomes.text: You arrange the job without charging. Your neighbor thanks you and offers help in return.

choices.text: Agree on a fair payment

outcomes.text: You agree on a price, arrange the work and receive the payment.

events.title: A traveler needs help
events.text: A traveler asks for help finding work. You can offer a meal, teach a task or introduce them to someone hiring.

choices.text: Share a meal and a little time

outcomes.text: You share food with the traveler and explain where they might find work.

choices.text: Teach something useful

outcomes.text: You demonstrate a useful task and let the traveler try it.

choices.text: Introduce the traveler to someone with work

outcomes.text: You introduce the traveler to someone hiring. They arrange a time to meet.

events.title: An agreement does not add up
events.text: The payment in an agreement is lower than you expected. Someone wants you to accept it quickly.

choices.text: Ask for a careful reading of the agreement

outcomes.text: A reader spots the missing payment before you accept the agreement.

choices.text: Ask someone trusted to help settle it

outcomes.text: A trusted person helps both sides agree on a revised payment.

choices.text: Leave the work and keep your time

outcomes.text: You leave without the payment and spend the time on other tasks.

events.title: Thinking about marriage
events.text: You consider looking for a partner. Open Your life to meet people, ask someone to court you or plan a wedding.

choices.text: Make room in your life to meet people

outcomes.text: You set aside time to meet people. You have not started a courtship yet.

choices.text: Keep your independence for now

outcomes.text: You decide against looking for a partner for now and focus on work and friends.

events.title: Thinking about a child
events.text: You and your spouse discuss having a child. Open Your life to try to grow your household; this conversation does not create a child.

choices.text: Talk through the work of care

outcomes.text: You and your spouse discuss feeding, care and how to divide the work.

choices.text: Keep your current household arrangements

outcomes.text: You decide not to try for a child now and keep your current household plans.

events.title: A friend asks about work
events.text: A younger friend wants help finding work. You could explain a few tasks or let them work beside you.

choices.text: Explain where to look for work

outcomes.text: You explain where to ask for work and how to handle a few common tasks.

choices.text: Let your friend work beside you

outcomes.text: Your friend works beside you for a while and helps finish an order.

events.title: A poor harvest
events.text: Reports of a poor harvest reach the city. Your household decides whether to store more food or share some supplies with relatives.

choices.text: Keep a small reserve for the household

outcomes.text: You buy a small reserve of food and store it at home.

choices.text: Share with the people closest to you

outcomes.text: You divide some supplies among relatives and keep less for your household.

events.title: New rules for work
events.text: Roman officials have changed some arrangements for work and agreements. You can ask about the new rules or get help from neighbors.

choices.text: Learn how the new arrangements work

outcomes.text: You ask about the new forms and learn which arrangements affect your work.

choices.text: Stay close to your established network

outcomes.text: Neighbors explain the new arrangements and help you find the right person to ask.

events.title: At forty
events.text: You turn forty. You have handled enough jobs and household problems to recognize some of them quickly.

events.title: An older relative needs help
events.text: An older relative needs help with meals and daily tasks. You must fit their care around paid work.

choices.text: Give more of your own time

outcomes.text: You miss some paid work to help your relative with meals and daily tasks.

choices.text: Arrange help across the household

outcomes.text: Several household members agree on times to help with the care.

events.title: Changing your workload
events.text: Carrying and lifting leave you tired for longer. You can take lighter tasks or keep working at the same pace.

choices.text: Take lighter tasks that need experience

outcomes.text: You take lighter tasks that need checking and advice rather than lifting.

choices.text: Keep taking the same jobs

outcomes.text: You keep taking the same jobs and earn more, but need longer to recover afterward.

events.title: Teaching a learner
events.text: A younger worker asks you to teach them. Lessons will take time away from your own orders.

choices.text: Teach the learner

outcomes.text: You show the learner each step and check their first attempts. Your own work takes longer.

choices.text: Finish your own orders

outcomes.text: You finish your own orders and make notes on the parts that need care.

events.title: Taking more rest
events.text: You have been slow to recover after work. You can take more days off or reduce your workload a little.

choices.text: Take more days off

outcomes.text: You take more days off. You earn less and recover some energy.

choices.text: Drop some demanding tasks

outcomes.text: You drop a few demanding tasks and keep the lighter paid work.

events.title: Leaving regular work
events.text: Your regular job is getting harder to manage. Leaving it will reduce your income, so your household will need to adjust.

choices.text: Leave your regular job

outcomes.text: You leave your regular job. You rest more and help with smaller household tasks.

choices.text: Keep some lighter work

outcomes.text: You keep some regular work and turn down the heavier tasks.

events.title: Arranging your belongings
events.text: You decide who should receive your belongings and settle your remaining obligations. You can record the arrangements or discuss them at home.

choices.text: Have the arrangements written down

outcomes.text: You pay for your instructions about belongings and obligations to be recorded.

choices.text: Discuss the arrangements at home

outcomes.text: You tell the household who should receive your belongings and how to settle your obligations.

events.title: Sorting papers and letters
events.text: You have a little time to help a younger person or sort the letters and papers you have kept.

choices.text: Show a beginner how to do a task

outcomes.text: You show a beginner how to handle a task and correct their first attempt.

choices.text: Sort your letters

outcomes.text: You sort your letters and label the ones you want to keep.

events.title: A visitor calls
events.text: A familiar visitor sits with you for a while. You can tell them a story or ask for their news.

choices.text: Tell a story about an old job

outcomes.text: You tell your visitor about an old job and answer a few questions.

choices.text: Ask for the visitor's news

outcomes.text: Your visitor tells you about work and the people at home.

events.title: An afternoon at home
events.text: You have a free afternoon. You can rest outside or ask someone to visit.

choices.text: Rest outside

outcomes.text: You sit outside for a while and return indoors when you get tired.

choices.text: Invite someone to visit

outcomes.text: A visitor joins you for a drink and stays through the afternoon.

events.title: An old neighbor's name
events.text: You mention an old neighbor. Someone asks where they lived, and you describe the house.

events.title: More help at home
events.text: At ninety, you need more help with meals, washing and moving around the house.

events.title: Your ninety-fifth year
events.text: You turn ninety-five. Your household helps with most daily tasks and makes sure you have company.

events.title: Resting at home
events.text: You spend much of the day resting. Someone brings water and leaves the door open for air.

events.title: A letter from a friend
events.text: A friend sends news from another town. You can pay to send a reply or put the letter aside for now.

choices.text: Send a reply

outcomes.text: You send a reply with your news and a few questions.

choices.text: Keep the message for another day

outcomes.text: You store the letter and leave the reply for another day.

events.title: An unwell week
events.text: You feel ill and have trouble finishing your work. You can ask someone to cover your tasks or do less until you recover.

choices.text: Accept help and rest

outcomes.text: Someone covers your tasks while you rest. You miss some pay but start to recover.

choices.text: Do what you can at a slower pace

outcomes.text: You finish a few smaller tasks and leave the rest until you feel better.

events.title: Recognizing voices
events.text: You recognize the people who care for you and turn when they call. They repeat the same names and songs through the day.

events.title: At the doorway
events.text: You watch people pass the doorway. An adult brings you back inside whenever you wander too far.

events.title: Meals and naps
events.text: Your caregivers fit meals and naps around their work. You object loudly when a meal is late.

events.title: More words
events.text: You learn a few more words and use them to ask for food, water and familiar people.

events.title: Sitting in the shade
events.text: Someone moves your seat out of the sun. You watch people carry baskets through the courtyard.

events.title: A familiar visitor
events.text: You recognize a visitor and reach toward them. They stop to talk and carry you for a while.

events.title: Knowing the way
events.text: You learn a shorter route to a nearby shop. You get there and back before the household starts looking for you.

events.title: Helping with small jobs
events.text: You carry small items, clear dishes and repeat messages. Adults still check the jobs before letting you go.

events.title: A smooth stone
events.text: You find a smooth stone and keep it in a pouch. Another child offers to trade for it, but you keep it.

events.title: A running joke
events.text: A friend makes everyone laugh during a game. You keep repeating the joke until the adults ask you to stop.

events.title: Trying a task
events.text: An adult lets you try part of a familiar task. They correct your grip and help you finish.

events.title: A longer errand
events.text: An errand takes you farther from home than usual. You find the right doorway and return with the delivery done.

events.title: Heavier loads
events.text: You can carry more than you could last year. People start asking you to help with heavier loads.

events.title: Trying again
events.text: You get a task wrong several times. After someone shows you slowly, you manage to finish it.

events.title: Talk after work
events.text: You listen while adults discuss prices and work. You ask about one detail and get a long explanation.

events.title: Different working hours
events.text: Your friends start keeping different working hours. You arrange to meet when everyone is free.

events.title: Delivering a message
events.text: Someone sends you with a message. You repeat it on the way so you will not forget part of it.

events.title: Asking about jobs
events.text: You ask workers how they learned their jobs. Some offer advice; others are too busy to stop.

events.title: The walk to work
events.text: You take the usual route to your job. A blocked lane makes you walk around the market on the way home.

events.title: Repairing a worn item
events.text: You repair a worn household item instead of replacing it. The repair holds after a few adjustments.

events.title: A long meal
events.text: Visitors stay after a meal to exchange news. You clear the dishes later than planned.

events.title: A busy week
events.text: Several jobs and household tasks need doing at once. You finish the urgent ones and leave the rest for later.

events.title: An hour off
events.text: You finish a task early and sit outside for a while. A neighbor stops to ask how the work went.

events.title: Asked to help again
events.text: Someone you helped before asks for another job. They give your name to a neighbor who also needs help.

events.title: Spotting a mistake
events.text: You notice a mistake before it causes more work. You show a younger worker what to check next time.

events.title: Starting later
events.text: You start a heavy task later and take an extra break. It is finished before evening.

events.title: A worker's suggestion
events.text: A younger worker suggests a different way to arrange a task. You try it and keep the part that saves time.

events.title: Moving things around
events.text: Your household moves bedding and storage jars to free some space. Everyone has to learn where things are now.

events.title: A delayed order
events.text: An order is delayed for several days. You work on smaller tasks until the materials arrive.

events.title: Meeting an old acquaintance
events.text: You meet someone you have not seen for years. You exchange news about work and people you both know.

events.title: An afternoon visitor
events.text: A visitor tells you about their household and stays for a drink. You ask them to come again next week.

events.title: Sorting a storage box
events.text: You sort a box of old belongings. Some are still useful, and some need cleaning or repair.

events.title: Help with a task
events.text: Someone offers to carry something that has become difficult for you. You let them take it and explain where it belongs.

events.title: News from the street
events.text: A visitor reports that a shop nearby has changed hands. You ask who is running it now.

events.title: Telling an old story
events.text: You tell a story about an old job. A listener asks a question, and you stop to explain the missing part.

events.title: Moving your chair
events.text: The sun reaches your usual seat earlier this season. Someone moves the chair into the shade.

events.title: News from another port
events.text: Someone mentions a port where you once worked. You ask whether the landing place is still used.

events.title: Checking some writing
events.text: You notice an unclear line on a page. You ask the writer to read it back before anyone copies it.

events.title: Greetings in the street
events.text: You stop several times on a short errand because neighbors want to talk. The errand takes longer than expected.

events.title: Sharing household tasks
events.text: You and your spouse divide the week's household tasks. One of you swaps a task to fit around paid work.

events.title: Your child needs different help
events.text: One of your children brings you a problem you have not handled before. You ask a few questions and work out how to help.

events.title: A friend needs help
events.text: A friend cannot finish a task. You can help, explain how to do it or return to your game.

choices.text: Stay and help

outcomes.text: You help your friend finish the task before returning to play.

choices.text: Show them what you know, then return to play

outcomes.text: You explain the next step and leave your friend to try it.

events.title: A free afternoon
events.text: There is no errand waiting this afternoon. You can watch a worker or find the other children.

choices.text: Watch how something is made

outcomes.text: A worker shows you the tools and answers your questions.

choices.text: Find the other children

outcomes.text: You find the other children and spend the afternoon playing.

events.title: An extra task
events.text: Someone offers you an extra task for a small payment. You had planned to meet people during the same hours.

choices.text: Try the unfamiliar work

outcomes.text: You complete the unfamiliar task and collect a small payment.

choices.text: Keep the time you promised to others

outcomes.text: You turn down the task and meet the people who were expecting you.

events.title: A question about work
events.text: You are stuck on part of a task. An experienced worker has time to explain it if you ask.

choices.text: Ask the question openly

outcomes.text: The worker explains the step you missed. Your next attempt goes better.

choices.text: Watch carefully before trying again

outcomes.text: You watch another attempt and practise the part that gave you trouble.

events.title: Lending a tool
events.text: A neighbor asks to borrow a tool you also need. You could rearrange your work or agree on a time to use it together.

choices.text: Lend it and rearrange your tasks

outcomes.text: Your neighbor returns the tool. You finish your own work later than planned.

choices.text: Offer a time when you can use it together

outcomes.text: You and your neighbor agree on a time to use the tool together.

events.title: Extra paid work
events.text: A small paid job is available. Taking it will leave less time for household tasks.

choices.text: Take the work this time

outcomes.text: You finish the job and bring home the payment. The household tasks wait.

choices.text: Keep the time for home

outcomes.text: You turn down the payment and finish the tasks at home.

events.title: Trying another method
events.text: Someone suggests a different way to finish a task. Trying it will take time and some material.

choices.text: Give the new method a careful try

outcomes.text: You try the new method and keep the steps that save work.

choices.text: Use the method you know well

outcomes.text: You use the method you know and finish without wasting material.

events.title: An invitation
events.text: An acquaintance invites you to a gathering. You could go or visit an old friend instead.

choices.text: Accept the invitation

outcomes.text: You meet several people at the gathering and exchange news about work.

choices.text: Make time for an old friend

outcomes.text: You visit your old friend and stay for a meal.

events.title: Two tasks at once
events.text: Someone asks for advice while you are finishing a task. You have enough energy to do one of them today.

choices.text: Help with the question

outcomes.text: You put your task aside and explain how you would handle the problem.

choices.text: Finish your task first

outcomes.text: You finish your task and arrange to talk another day.

events.title: A question about an old place
events.text: A visitor asks about a place where you once lived. You can describe it or ask someone to write down the details.

choices.text: Describe the place

outcomes.text: You describe the place and answer questions about who lived there.

choices.text: Have the details written down

outcomes.text: Someone writes down the place names and details you want to keep.

events.title: A short outing
events.text: Someone offers to walk with you on a short visit. You could go or invite a visitor to come to your home.

choices.text: Go together, at an easy pace

outcomes.text: You make the short visit, take a break and return home together.

choices.text: Invite a visitor to come to you

outcomes.text: You stay at home and ask your visitor to come over instead.

events.title: An item you no longer use
events.text: You find an item you seldom use. Someone else could use it, but you might still want to keep it.

choices.text: Give the item away

outcomes.text: You give the item to someone who can use it.

choices.text: Keep it for your own use

outcomes.text: You keep the item and explain when you still use it.

events.title: Porridge on the floor
events.text: You knock over your bowl. Someone cleans the floor and gives you a smaller serving.

events.title: A patched blanket
events.text: A relative patches your blanket. You pull at the new stitching until they move your hand.

events.title: A noisy visitor
events.text: A visitor makes you laugh by copying animal sounds. You keep asking for the goat again.

events.title: A chipped cup
events.text: You chip a cup while clearing a meal. An adult shows you how to carry fewer things at once.

events.title: The missing goat
events.text: A neighbor's goat gets loose. You spot it chewing a basket and call for its owner.

events.title: Counting the change
events.text: You bring home the right change from an errand. Your household lets you check the coins yourself.

events.title: Pigeons on the roof
events.text: You and a friend watch pigeons crowd around a rooftop. The owner comes out and chases them away.

events.title: A queue at the bakery
events.text: The bakery opens late. You wait with the other customers and get home after your household expected you.

events.title: A borrowed writing tablet
events.text: A neighbor lends you a tablet for an afternoon. You copy a short list and wipe it clean before returning it.

events.title: A cart blocks the lane
events.text: A cart loses a wheel in a narrow lane. You help shift its baskets so people can get past.

events.title: Dearer bread
events.text: Bread costs more at your usual stall. You buy a smaller loaf and add beans to the meal.

events.title: Cloudy water
events.text: The water in a household jar looks dirty. You empty it, scrub the jar and fetch another load.

events.title: A missing tool
events.text: You spend a morning looking for a tool. It turns up under a folded cloth where you left it.

events.title: A leak after rain
events.text: Rain gets through a crack in the roof. You move a basket and patch the gap before the next shower.

events.title: Waiting at the quay
events.text: Several ships arrive together. The quay stays crowded while porters argue over where to put the cargo.

events.title: A loose hinge
events.text: A door scrapes the floor. You tighten its fittings and ask someone to lift it while you check the gap.

events.title: Checking a measure
events.text: A seller's grain measure looks smaller than yours. You compare them before agreeing on the price.

events.title: A late payment
events.text: Someone pays you later than agreed. You spend less for a few days until the money arrives.

events.title: Mended sandals
events.text: A strap comes loose from your sandal. A neighbor repairs it while you wait nearby.

events.title: A better seat
events.text: A visitor brings a low stool so you can sit outside more comfortably. You return it after the afternoon meal.

events.title: The key turns up
events.text: You cannot find a small key. After checking the room twice, you find it inside a bowl.

events.title: A short visit
events.text: A relative walks with you to a nearby temple. You rest in the shade before heading home.

events.title: A coin in the dust
events.text: You find a coin where a seller has just packed up. They are still close enough to call.

choices.text: Call the seller back

outcomes.text: The seller thanks you and checks the rest of the purse.

choices.text: Take the coin home

outcomes.text: You bring the coin home. Nobody comes looking for it.

events.title: A broken clay toy
events.text: A toy breaks during a game. You can try to mend it or ask the other children to play something else.

choices.text: Try to mend it

outcomes.text: The toy looks crooked, but the pieces hold together.

choices.text: Start another game

outcomes.text: You leave the pieces aside and get everyone playing again.

events.title: An errand across town
events.text: A trader offers a small payment for a delivery. It will take most of the afternoon.

choices.text: Take the delivery

outcomes.text: You get the parcel there on time and collect your payment.

choices.text: Keep your afternoon free

outcomes.text: The trader finds someone else. You spend the afternoon with friends.

events.title: A cheap used tool
events.text: A worker offers to sell you an old tool. It needs cleaning, but it could be useful for practice.

choices.text: Buy and repair it

outcomes.text: You clean the tool and replace a worn fitting before using it.

choices.text: Borrow one when you need it

outcomes.text: A neighbor agrees to lend you a tool for short tasks.

events.title: Space at a market stall
events.text: A seller has room on a stall for a few extra goods. You can pay for the space or help carry the stock instead.

choices.text: Pay for space and sell a small batch

outcomes.text: Some goods sell quickly and some come home with you.

choices.text: Help the seller for a day's pay

outcomes.text: You carry stock, pack the stall and receive the agreed payment.

events.title: Work next door
events.text: A neighbor starts noisy repairs before sunrise. You have a long day ahead and want more sleep.

choices.text: Ask them to start later

outcomes.text: You agree on quieter hours for the next few mornings.

choices.text: Move your sleeping place for now

outcomes.text: You shift your bedding to a quieter corner until the repairs finish.

events.title: Smoke from a warehouse
events.text: Smoke comes from a warehouse doorway. Someone inside calls for help. Going through the smoke could kill you; people outside are forming a bucket line.

choices.text: Stay outside and pass water

outcomes.text: You pass buckets while others clear the nearby buildings.

choices.text: Go inside to help — risk of death

outcomes.text: You reach the person and help them out. You spend days coughing after the smoke.
Heat forces you back. Burns keep you away from work while others care for you.
You enter the warehouse, but the smoke overcomes you before you can get out.

events.title: A rough crossing
events.text: Bad weather is approaching. The master offers extra pay to sail now, but the crew could wait in port. Leaving in this weather could be fatal.

choices.text: Wait in port

outcomes.text: The ship stays moored until the weather improves. You lose the extra payment.

choices.text: Sail for extra pay — risk of death

outcomes.text: The crossing is rough, but the ship reaches port. You collect the extra pay and need a long rest.
A wave sweeps you over the side during the crossing. The crew cannot reach you in time.

events.title: Robbers in a narrow lane
events.text: Two people block your path and demand your purse. You can hand it over and leave. Trying to fight them could be fatal.

choices.text: Hand over the purse and leave

outcomes.text: They take the purse and let you go. You reach home unhurt.

choices.text: Try to fight them — risk of death

outcomes.text: You shout and push past them. Other people arrive before they can follow.
One of the robbers wounds you during the fight. You do not survive the injury.

events.title: Water in a dirty jar
events.text: Your stored water smells wrong. Replacing it will cost time and money. Drinking it could cause a serious, sometimes fatal illness.

choices.text: Empty the jar and fetch fresh water

outcomes.text: You scrub the jar and replace the water before the next meal.

choices.text: Use it anyway — risk of fatal illness

outcomes.text: You use the water and notice no illness afterward.
You fall ill after using the water and miss several days of work.
You become severely ill after using the water. You grow weaker and do not recover.

events.title: A repair overhead
events.text: A roof tile is loose. A worker can repair it, or a relative can help you arrange a cheaper patch from inside.

choices.text: Pay a worker to fix it

outcomes.text: The worker secures the tile and checks the tiles beside it.

choices.text: Ask for help with an inside patch

outcomes.text: You and a relative stop the drip until a full repair can be made.

events.title: Vegetables to prepare
events.text: A neighbor brings vegetables to prepare for a meal. You could help with the cutting or contribute some ingredients.

choices.text: Help prepare the meal

outcomes.text: You sit together and finish the vegetables before the pot is ready.

choices.text: Contribute ingredients instead

outcomes.text: You add a few things from your stores and rest while the others cook.

events.title: Checking a kiln load
events.text: You inspect a cooled kiln load. A few pieces are cracked; the rest can be finished for sale.

events.title: A fitting that works
events.text: A repaired wooden fitting holds when you test it. The customer asks you to make another.

events.title: A customer changes the design
events.text: A customer asks for another detail on a small figure. It will take extra time and material.

choices.text: Agree on extra pay and add the detail

outcomes.text: You agree on the price, revise the figure and finish later than planned.

choices.text: Finish the original order

outcomes.text: You finish the design that was agreed and deliver it on time.

events.title: An objection at a discussion
events.text: Someone challenges a claim you have made. They ask you to show how you reached it.

choices.text: Explain the steps and accept questions

outcomes.text: You explain the steps. A question exposes a gap, and you revise part of the argument.

choices.text: Write down the objection and review it later

outcomes.text: You record the objection and compare it with the text after the meeting.

events.title: A clear night
events.text: The sky clears after several cloudy evenings. You add an observation to your record and compare it with the last entry.

events.title: Two different chart readings
events.text: Two readers give different interpretations of the same sky diagram. You can compare their calculations or ask how they chose their rules.

choices.text: Check the positions and arithmetic

outcomes.text: You find a copied position that differs between the charts and record the correction.

choices.text: Compare the interpretation rules

outcomes.text: You list the rules each reader used. The exercise records their beliefs without proving either prediction.

events.title: Orders during the Alexandrian War
events.text: Fighting has reached Alexandria. Your unit needs people to protect stores and a smaller group for a forward post. The forward post carries a risk of death.

choices.text: Guard the stores and move supplies

outcomes.text: You guard the stores and help move supplies away from a threatened lane.

choices.text: Volunteer for the forward post (risk of death)

outcomes.text: You return from the post with a damaged shield and a better understanding of the unit's movements.
You are wounded while holding the forward post. You do not survive the injury.

events.title: The unit checks its equipment
events.text: During the continuing fighting, your unit guards a storehouse. You check equipment and count incoming supply loads.

events.title: Your first unit orders
events.text: You write a guard rota, check the equipment list and explain the next day's tasks to your unit.

events.title: A command decision about supplies
events.text: Your staff cannot provide the same escort for every route. You must decide whether to protect the district's grain stores or escort the next supply convoy.

choices.text: Assign troops to protect the grain stores

outcomes.text: Your troops take posts at the stores. Clerks report that deliveries can be unloaded there without interruption.

choices.text: Assign troops to escort the supply convoy

outcomes.text: Your escort brings the convoy through. Other units receive their loads on the planned day.

events.title: The new grain order is carried out
events.text: Clerks use the schedule you proposed. Grain is delivered to the district storehouses you named, and the delivery lists are checked against your plan.

events.title: Your royal appointment ends
events.text: Roman rule replaces the Ptolemaic administration. Your royal army or court appointment ends. You keep your training and contacts, but must find other work.

events.title: Comparing a temple sky diagram
events.text: A copied sky diagram is brought for study. You compare its zodiacal signs with other notes and record the differences. Access to this copy is part of the fictional story.

endings.title: Death in infancy
endings.text: You die before your first birthday. Your household arranges your funeral.

endings.title: Death in childhood
endings.text: You die during childhood. Your household arranges your funeral.

endings.title: Death in adulthood
endings.text: You die as an adult. Your household arranges your funeral and deals with your unfinished work.

endings.title: Death in later life
endings.text: You die in later life. Your household arranges your funeral and sorts your belongings.

sources.title: Strabo, Geography 17.1.3–10: the Nile and Alexandria
sources.publisher: LacusCurtius, University of Chicago; H. L. Jones, Loeb translation (1932)
sources.period: Augustan-era account of Egypt and Alexandria, referring also to earlier Ptolemaic history
sources.summary: Describes Alexandria's harbors, Pharos, streets and royal district, and the importance of Nile inundation, canals and agricultural management.
sources.limitations: Elite literary testimony with Roman imperial sympathies. Descriptive claims and reported numbers are not a population survey, an exact city map or annual household probabilities.

sources.title: Bellum Alexandrinum 1–33: the Alexandrian War
sources.publisher: LacusCurtius, University of Chicago; Loeb translation (1955)
sources.period: Events of 48–47 BCE; authorship traditionally associated with the Caesarian corpus
sources.summary: Narrates fighting, barricades, harbor operations and disruption of Caesar's water supply during the Alexandrian War.
sources.limitations: A partisan Roman military narrative with prejudicial descriptions of Alexandrians. It supports a war setting, not invented civilian experiences, precise casualty odds or a claim that the entire Library was destroyed.

sources.title: Chronological Tables for Caesar's Wars (58–45 BCE)
sources.publisher: John T. Ramsey and Kurt A. Raaflaub, Histos 11 (2017); journal page published online 2018
sources.period: 58–45 BCE, including the Alexandrian War of 48–47 BCE
sources.geography: Roman campaigns including Alexandria and Egypt
sources.summary: Reconstructs the sequence of Caesar's campaigns and separates Roman civil-calendar dates from reconstructed Julian dates.
sources.limitations: A scholarly chronology reconstructed from ancient testimony. Day-level dates may be disputed; the game uses year-level anchors and does not reproduce whole tables.

sources.title: Ptolemaic Period
sources.publisher: Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities
sources.period: 332–30 BCE; Actium in 31 BCE and the end of Ptolemaic rule in 30 BCE
sources.summary: Provides a heritage-authority overview of Ptolemaic Egypt and the transition following the defeat at Actium.
sources.limitations: A broad public-history overview, not a detailed social dataset. Use the year-level chronology without treating its compressed narrative as proof of every personal consequence.

sources.title: Augustus, Res Gestae, especially section 27
sources.publisher: Livius.org; F. W. Shipley translation from LacusCurtius
sources.period: Augustus's retrospective inscription, completed near the end of his reign in 14 CE
sources.geography: Roman Empire; section 27 concerns annexation of Egypt
sources.summary: Augustus claims to have added Egypt to Roman rule. The inscription offers a contemporary imperial voice for the political transition.
sources.limitations: Self-promotional imperial testimony. It does not describe the response of all Egyptians and must be paired with independent chronology and local evidence.

sources.title: Alexandrian Documents from the Reign of Augustus
sources.publisher: Peter van Minnen, Department of Classics, University of Cincinnati
sources.period: Augustan Alexandria, especially 13 BCE; individual texts and later additions have their own dates
sources.geography: Documents issued in Alexandria, many recovered from reused cartonnage at Abusir el-Melek
sources.summary: Provides scholarly English translations of Alexandrian contracts, letters, petitions and association records, with document identifiers and links to the underlying Greek texts.
sources.limitations: The surviving archive is selective, not representative of every household. Early Roman material is comparative evidence for earlier Ptolemaic years; use each document's actual date.

sources.title: BGU 4.1125.1–15: apprenticeship contract for a musician
sources.publisher: Peter van Minnen, University of Cincinnati, translation of the primary papyrus
sources.period: March/April 13 BCE
sources.summary: Records training in flute playing, the term of apprenticeship, provision of food and clothing, and examination by fellow practitioners.
sources.limitations: The apprentice is enslaved, and this is a specific musical contract. It is evidence for organized training, not universal schooling or the terms of a free child's scribal apprenticeship.

sources.title: BGU 4.1058: wetnursing contract
sources.publisher: Peter van Minnen, University of Cincinnati, translation of the primary papyrus
sources.period: 30 March 13 BCE
sources.summary: Documents paid nursing, infant care and a clause anticipating the possibility of a child's death.
sources.limitations: Both nurse and infant are enslaved in this contract. Its clauses show contemporary concerns; they do not estimate infant mortality or demonstrate that every household employed a wet nurse.

sources.title: BGU 4.1052.1–34: marriage contract
sources.publisher: Peter van Minnen, University of Cincinnati, translation of the primary papyrus
sources.period: 15 April 13 BCE
sources.summary: Records an agreement for a shared life, a dowry and economic and marital obligations.
sources.limitations: One Greek-language legal agreement, with particular status and guardianship conventions. Its terms are not universal Egyptian marriage rules or an observed marriage-age distribution.

sources.title: BGU 4.1141: private letter
sources.publisher: Peter van Minnen, University of Cincinnati, translation of the primary papyrus
sources.period: After 9 April 13 BCE
sources.summary: Preserves correspondence concerning friendship, accusations, work, wages and interpersonal obligations.
sources.limitations: A fragmentary and sometimes difficult personal letter, embedded in unequal relationships. It supports written communication as a theme, not the fictional character's letter or a literacy rate.

sources.title: BGU 4.1117: lease contract for a bakery
sources.publisher: Peter van Minnen, University of Cincinnati, translation of the primary papyrus
sources.period: April/May 13 BCE
sources.summary: Describes a bakery lease, equipment, rent, repairs and responsibility for taxes, illustrating workshop livelihoods and contractual obligations.
sources.limitations: A single bakery agreement. Monetary amounts and conditions cannot be generalized to all trades or converted directly into the game's abstract wealth score.

sources.title: BGU 4.1151.1–18: partial payment of an inheritance
sources.publisher: Peter van Minnen, University of Cincinnati, translation of the primary papyrus
sources.period: 12 April 13 BCE
sources.summary: Records an agreement concerning the partial payment of an inheritance, supporting a narrative theme of property and obligations between generations.
sources.limitations: A particular legal settlement. It supplies neither a representative inheritance amount nor evidence that all older people held transferable property.

sources.title: Education and Apprenticeship
sources.publisher: Nikolaos Lazaridis (2010), UCLA Encyclopedia of Egyptology
sources.period: Survey across ancient Egyptian periods, including Ptolemaic and Roman bilingual education
sources.summary: Reviews training for scribes and specialist crafts, educational exercises and restricted access to formal schooling.
sources.limitations: A long-period synthesis with uneven evidence. It cannot supply exact Alexandrian enrolment or literacy probabilities, and does not justify giving every child formal schooling.

sources.title: Funerary Rituals (Ptolemaic and Roman Periods)
sources.publisher: Christina Riggs (2010), UCLA Encyclopedia of Egyptology; University of East Anglia repository
sources.period: Ptolemaic and Roman periods
sources.geography: Egypt; evidence includes Akhmim, Thebes, Tuna el-Gebel and other communities
sources.summary: Surveys burial, commemoration, mourning and funerary associations, including arrangements for members to contribute to funeral costs.
sources.limitations: Rites varied with community, status, resources and religion. Elite mummification evidence is not a universal Alexandrian funeral script; use broad remembrance themes carefully.

sources.title: The abuse of aged parents in the ancient Roman world
sources.publisher: Tim Parkin, Bulletin of the Institute of Classical Studies 66(2), 41–50; online 2024
sources.period: Roman world with Ptolemaic Egyptian petitions of 225 and 221 BCE among the comparative cases
sources.geography: Roman Mediterranean and the Arsinoite nome in Egypt
sources.summary: Examines duties, dependence and care between generations, including papyrus petitions by older parents.
sources.limitations: Sparse, often one-sided dispute evidence from varied times and places. It does not establish rates of neglect or a uniform old-age household arrangement in Alexandria.

sources.title: Volcanic suppression of Nile summer flooding triggers revolt and constrains interstate conflict in ancient Egypt
sources.publisher: Joseph G. Manning and colleagues (2017), Nature Communications 8, 900; author copy at UC Berkeley
sources.period: Ptolemaic Egypt, 305–30 BCE, with later Nilometer measurements used for comparison
sources.geography: Nile basin and Egypt; papyrus survival particularly strong in the Fayyum
sources.summary: Combines environmental reconstructions and ancient writings to examine Nile flood variability, agricultural vulnerability and social stress.
sources.limitations: Ancient flood indications are intermittent and may have dating uncertainty. The continuous Nilometer series begins in 622 CE; this is not a precise annual Alexandrian food-price or famine-risk dataset.

sources.title: Roman Model Life Table (Coale–Demeny Female West Level 3)
sources.publisher: Columbia University / W. V. Harris teaching resources
sources.period: Comparative Roman demographic model; not an observed Ptolemaic cohort
sources.geography: Roman comparison model; not an Alexandria-specific dataset
sources.summary: Provides age-band mortality, survivorship and remaining life expectancy for a model population with life expectancy at birth of 25 years.
sources.limitations: A female model life table, not measured male Alexandrian rates. Converting interval death probabilities into annual hazards assumes within-band timing. Age at death is simulated, not a historical prediction.

sources.title: Quantifying antiquity
sources.publisher: Roger S. Bagnall, Columbia University
sources.period: Contrasts Roman Egyptian census evidence with Hellenistic Egyptian household lists
sources.summary: Explains the promise and limits of ancient demographic evidence, including why Hellenistic household lists without ages cannot yield life expectancy.
sources.limitations: A methodological essay rather than a downloadable life table. It explicitly cautions against combining Roman and Hellenistic evidence without careful analysis.

sources.title: Life Expectancy
sources.publisher: Sonia Zakrzewski (2015), UCLA Encyclopedia of Egyptology
sources.period: Long-period review of ancient Egyptian demographic evidence, including Roman model tables
sources.geography: Egypt; evidence from varied populations and sites
sources.summary: Explains demographic methods and biases. Table 1 reproduces a model life table for Roman Egyptian females after Bagnall and Frier (1994), with life expectancy at birth of 22.5 years.
sources.limitations: A later-period female model inferred using census returns and Coale–Demeny West, not observed mortality for a male in Ptolemaic Alexandria. Annual interpolation and the final age-band policy are additional game assumptions; cause-of-death rates are not supplied.

sources.title: Zodiaque de Dendéra (E 13482)
sources.publisher: Musée du Louvre, Egyptian Antiquities collection
sources.period: 50 BCE; catalogue dates the relief to June–August
sources.summary: Catalogues a sandstone ceiling relief with zodiacal signs, decans and constellations, providing a contemporary example of Egyptian astral imagery.
sources.limitations: A temple object from Dendera, not an Alexandrian teaching manual. It supplies neither access probabilities nor evidence that astrological predictions were reliable.

sources.title: Alexandrian terracottas
sources.publisher: Vatican Museums, Gregorian Egyptian Museum
sources.period: Ptolemaic and Roman periods
sources.geography: Alexandria; collection objects have varied acquisition histories
sources.summary: Describes Alexandrian figurative terracottas, including mould-made examples and a range of decorative and religious subjects.
sources.limitations: The collection spans multiple periods and some objects entered through the antiquities market. It does not measure workshop employment, wages or apprenticeship access.

sources.title: Statuette of an ancestral king (2003.154)
sources.publisher: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.period: Late Period–Early Ptolemaic Period, 380–246 BCE
sources.geography: Egypt; exact workshop not established in this catalogue entry
sources.summary: Documents a carved wooden ritual figure associated with temple equipment, illustrating skilled Egyptian wood carving.
sources.limitations: Earlier than the player's lifetime and not specifically Alexandrian. The object's interpretation is debated; it does not establish a universal carving curriculum or job ladder.

sources.title: An enigmatic early horoscope: BKT X 29 (P. 11831)
sources.publisher: Berlin Papyrus Database, Egyptian Museum and Papyrus Collection; Marius Gerhardt, Andreas Winkler and Michael Zellmann-Rohrer
sources.period: Late Ptolemaic or early Roman handwriting; astronomical reconstruction best fits 5 June 29 BCE
sources.summary: Examines a Greek horoscope listing astral positions, abbreviations, the ascendant and midheaven, with possible professional or client use.
sources.limitations: The papyrus lacks a personal name and explicit date, and its solar position conflicts with the proposed reconstruction. Its use is uncertain, and no accompanying interpretation survives.

sources.title: Plutarch, Life of Antony 80: Areius and Octavian at Alexandria
sources.publisher: LacusCurtius, University of Chicago; Bernadotte Perrin, Loeb translation
sources.period: Later biography describing the Roman takeover of Alexandria in 30 BCE
sources.summary: Depicts the philosopher Areius receiving public favour from Octavian and interceding for others, illustrating elite intellectual patronage and political access.
sources.limitations: A retrospective literary account, not an administrative record or promotion dataset. It concerns an exceptional elite figure and does not prove ordinary access to Cleopatra's court.
